target_customer: Frontier AI labs buying benchmarks, training data and RL environments for electrical engineering
problem: AI models are weak at real electrical engineering that mixes simulation, bench measurements and physical constraints, and labs lack realistic evals and training environments for it.
business_model: Sales of benchmarks, training data and RL environments to AI labs
product_category: AI evals and RL environments for hardware engineering

founders.name: Trishala Jain
education: UC Berkeley, EECS and MET (per YC page)

competitors.name: HWE-Bench
competitors.what: Benchmark of 300 board-level circuit design tasks across 8 domains for AI models

competitors.name: EEBench (atopile)
competitors.what: Benchmark testing agents on electrical engineering design tasks
competitors.traction_then: Public leaderboard with several frontier models

competitors.name: Standard Machines
competitors.what: YC company selling RL environments and evals for AI chip design

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining design, simulation and physical lab experiments into benchmarks and RL environments needs hardware lab work plus ML evaluation expertise from a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Benchmarks are copyable by labs or academics, and the physical lab workflow data is the only plausible moat; none shown yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet observable; the company is in the Fall 2026 batch and no incumbent action was found.

market_need_then: Frontier labs were spending on RL environments in 2025 and 2026 and new electrical engineering benchmarks (HWE-Bench, EEBench) appeared, showing demand for realistic hardware evals.

identity.logo: Not examined beyond text wordmark on site
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and research oriented, asks for expert contributors

brand_strength.rationale: Little public brand evidence; a search for the name returns other Evident companies, so the generic name may cause confusion.

outcome_analysis: Evident Machines is a two person Fall 2026 YC company with no public funding, exit or traction data, so no outcome can be judged yet. The team pairs Google and Berkeley AI research backgrounds with a San Francisco lab, and the wedge is benchmarks and RL environments for electrical engineering, an area where competing benchmarks appeared in 2026.
notes: No funding found in a funding search; the search returned unrelated companies named EVident Battery and Evident Systems. No second funding source exists. No outcome events found. Competitor dates reflect 2026 sources near the batch.
